answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by making each identity post a non-refundable stake, slashed on proven duplication. Before transacting, an agent registers a fingerprint of its signing key in a shared registry, so peers verify every message against that record instead of trusting a fresh name. Faking ten thousand agents means funding ten thousand stakes, so cost scales linearly while payoff does not. The record stays under an opaque onyx seal, uniqueness is proven inside a cipher of commitments, and disputes post the archive under an umber stamp. Throwaway keys cannot pay the stake.
